note: HCV grows in no ordinary lab animal, so the NS5A class was discovered, dosed and genotype-stratified on the Huh-7 replicon, whose resistance map later let regulators pick which patients need testing or longer therapy.
label: HCV NS5A inhibitors

engagement.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; J Virol print Jan 2010, online-ahead-of-print date not verified.
engagement.judgement: Opener at the first peer-reviewed use of the replicon for this class; the tile's members descend from this BMS-824 series (Gao 2010).
engagement.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 cells; genotype 1a/1b and patient-derived NS5A hybrid replicons)
engagement.note: A replicon screen found the NS5A chemotype (BMS-824, EC50 ~5 nM) and mapped resistance to L31V/Y93H; no patient data yet.
engagement.quote: Using a cell-based replicon screen, we identified a class of compounds with a thiazolidinone core structure as inhibitors of hepatitis C virus (HCV) replication.

engagement.magnitude_basis: plasma HCV RNA decline (3.3 log10 at 24 h) vs picomolar replicon EC50; different quantities, direction only
engagement.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the same paper reports replicon EC50s and the patient viral-load fall, so comparison_stated is true.
engagement.judgement: Viral load is the target's own product, so this is engagement at the proximal tier, not efficacy (no SVR). Same-year opener and comparison, as in the v2 NS3/4A entry.
engagement.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 cells; genotype 1a/1b and patient-derived NS5A hybrid replicons)
engagement.note: Daclatasvir, picomolar in replicons, cut plasma HCV RNA 3.3 log10 within 24 h of a single 100-mg dose in genotype 1b patients.
engagement.short: Single dose cuts HCV RNA 3.3 log10
engagement.quote: In a phase I clinical trial in patients chronically infected with HCV, administration of a single 100-mg dose of BMS-790052 was associated with a 3.3 log(10) reduction in mean viral load measured 24 h post-dose

engagement.magnitude_basis: identity of resistance substitutions (28/30/31/93 in 1a; 31/93 in 1b) and the 1a-vs-1b rebound pattern
engagement.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the paper's title states the in-vitro/in-vivo correlation. Patient-level because it predicts which subtypes and variants keep responding.
engagement.judgement: Placed in engagement rather than efficacy: loss of the PD readout on monotherapy is not a trial primary endpoint. Corroborated by Nettles 2011 (doi:10.1002/hep.24609), whose abstract says rebound variants were those 'previously implicated in resistance development in the in vitro replicon system'.
engagement.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 cells; genotype 1a/1b and patient-derived NS5A hybrid replicons)
engagement.note: On 14-day monotherapy the variants that broke through (28/30/31/93 in 1a; 31/93 in 1b) were the ones the replicon had selected; 1a rebounded more, as predicted.
engagement.short: Patient escape variants match replicon map
engagement.quote: Analyses of the sequence variants (1) established a correlation between resistant variants emerging in vivo with BMS-790052 treatment and those observed in the in vitro replicon system
engagement.reason: Replicon potency and resistance map held

dose.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
dose.judgement: Opener; the dose comparison needs multiple-dose PK, which came in 2011.
dose.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 cells; genotype 1a/1b and patient-derived NS5A hybrid replicons)
dose.note: Picomolar replicon EC50 set the exposure target; a single-dose study showed activity but no steady-state exposure comparison yet.
dose.quote: Here we describe the profile of BMS-790052, a small molecule inhibitor of the HCV NS5A protein that exhibits picomolar half-maximum effective concentrations (EC(50)) towards replicons expressing a broad range of HCV genotypes

dose.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paired by me (model side Gao 2010 replicon EC50s). The trough-over-protein-adjusted-EC50 ratio is in the paper body and not re-read, so magnitude is left null. The MAD study's NCT number was not looked up.
dose.judgement: Scored 'reached, drug worked': the replicon-derived exposure was reached at doses that gave near-maximal viral decline, and the 60-mg dose chosen here cured patients in Lok 2012 and ALLY-3. margin_stated left null: the animal NOAELs (rat 1-month AUC 5.07 ug.h/mL) sit near or below the human 60-mg AUC, so no tolerated-above-effective margin was asserted in the sources quoted.
dose.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 cells; genotype 1a/1b and patient-derived NS5A hybrid replicons)
dose.note: Fourteen-day dosing at 1-100 mg gave 2.8-4.1 log10 maximal HCV RNA declines with once-daily PK; 60 mg was carried forward and later cured patients.
dose.quote: At doses of 1-100 mg daily, BMS-790052 was well tolerated, had a PK profile supportive of once-daily dosing, and produced a rapid and substantial decrease in HCV-RNA levels in patients chronically infected with HCV genotype 1.

dose.magnitude_basis: SVR12 flat across the daclatasvir exposure range at 60 mg (exposure on the plateau)
dose.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
dose.confidence_note: Read in the bundled review text. Paired by me with the label's replicon EC50 table (model side, tier 2); the review's Phase 3 data are the daclatasvir + asunaprevir trials.
dose.judgement: Strengthening entry: a flat exposure-response at the registered dose is the regulator's statement that exposure exceeded what was needed. The same review notes lower SVR12 with baseline Y93H/L31 variants, which is the efficacy cell's patient-level story, not a dose failure.
dose.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 cells; genotype 1a/1b and patient-derived NS5A hybrid replicons)
dose.note: FDA found no exposure-response for SVR12 across the daclatasvir range at 60 mg: the dose sits on the plateau the replicon potency implied.
dose.short: FDA: SVR flat across exposure at 60 mg
dose.quote: No major differences were identified across the asunaprevir or daclatasvir exposure range in evaluating the exposure-response relationship for efficacy when the overall information from the Phase 3 trials was analyzed.
dose.reason: Target reached with room; drug cured

efficacy.note: Replicon selection mapped NS5A resistance (L31V, Y93H) before any patient was dosed; SVR untested.
efficacy.quote: Replicon cells resistant to BMS-824 were isolated, and mutations were identified.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: SVR12 achieved vs replicon prediction of potency with a low 1a barrier; 2/2 1b cured, 6 1a breakthroughs
efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Primary endpoint SVR12 per the abstract; registry record (first posted 2009-11-13) lists HCV RNA levels as the primary measure and has no posted results. Paired by me with Gao 2010.
efficacy.judgement: First trial with SVR as primary endpoint for a member drug. Class-level 'same': the replicon predicted potency and a lower 1a barrier (Fridell 2010/2011), and the trial showed both. Not 'neg' because no member drug failed in patients for lack of replicon activity.
efficacy.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 cells; genotype 1a/1b and patient-derived NS5A hybrid replicons)
efficacy.note: Daclatasvir + asunaprevir cured null responders without interferon (SVR12 4/11 dual, 10/10 quad); 1a breakthroughs carried NS5A resistance, as the replicon predicted.
efficacy.short: Dual DAA cures; 1a escapes as predicted
efficacy.quote: This preliminary study involving patients with HCV genotype 1 infection who had not had a response to prior therapy showed that a sustained virologic response can be achieved with two direct-acting antiviral agents only.

patient_trials.quote: A total of 4 patients in group A (36%; 2 of 9 with HCV genotype 1a and 2 of 2 with genotype 1b) had a sustained virologic response at 12 weeks after treatment and also at 24 weeks after treatment.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: eradication with NS5A + NS3 (or NS5B) combination vs breakthrough on monotherapy, in genotype 1b
efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The NS5A compound was BMS-788329, a daclatasvir sibling, not a member drug (product_in_model false). The abstract does not cite Lok 2012, so the pairing is mine.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track: a different system (infected animal) with its own prediction. Scored retrodiction because the human answer (dual DAA cures 1b; monotherapy selects resistance) was public from Lok 2012 (Jan 2012) before this appeared (Jan 2013); the mouse experiments may have run earlier, but no source dates them. Its genotype 2a/2b failure in mice was never tested with a member drug in patients, so no prospective entry follows.
efficacy.model: Human-liver chimeric uPA/SCID mouse infected with HCV genotype 1b, 2a or 2b
efficacy.note: A year after Lok 2012, humanized mice given a sibling NS5A inhibitor reproduced the clinic: monotherapy bred resistant breakthrough, NS5A + NS3 combination eradicated genotype 1b.
efficacy.quote: In contrast to monotherapy, 4 weeks of combination therapy with the NS5A RCI and either NS3 PI or NS5B inhibitor succeeded in completely eradicating the virus in genotype 1b HCV-infected mice.

patient_trials.quote: All 10 patients in group B had a sustained virologic response at 12 weeks after treatment, and 9 had a sustained virologic response at 24 weeks after treatment.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: Y93H: 2,737-fold replicon shift vs SVR12 54% (7/13) with vs 92% (124/135) without
efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.confidence_note: Label section 12.4 read in full from the bundled text; the replicon fold-shifts and the ALLY-3 SVR12 table sit side by side there. Nelson 2015 (ALLY-3 primary paper) verified by PubMed title only; the patient_trials quote is the label's Table 7 row, not Nelson's text.
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level prediction: the replicon's largest shift (Y93H) was the only baseline polymorphism that lowered SVR12; the smaller shifts (A30K 56-fold, S62L 1.75-fold) did not, which the same section reports. Scored as 'match' because the FDA pairs the two in one section; it does not use the words 'as predicted'.
efficacy.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 cells; genotype 1a/1b and patient-derived NS5A hybrid replicons)
efficacy.note: Y93H, a 2,737-fold shift in the genotype 3a replicon, cut SVR12 from 92% to 54% in ALLY-3 (25% in cirrhotics); other replicon-flagged positions did not.
efficacy.short: Replicon Y93H shift predicts GT3 failures
efficacy.quote: The Y93H polymorphism was detected in 9% (13/148) of subjects receiving DAKLINZA and sofosbuvir and was associated with reduced SVR12 rates (Table 7).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: replicon-defined NS5A positions 28/30/31/93 (elbasvir shifts 1.5- to 2,000-fold in 1a) vs SVR12 70% (39/56) with vs 98% (441/450) without
efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.confidence_note: Label section 12.4 read in full from the bundled text (pooled Phase 2/3; C-EDGE TN NCT02105467 is the pivotal study, results posted 2016-04-12). The patient_trials quote is the label's Table 11, flattened.
efficacy.judgement: Second regulator use of the replicon at patient level: the positions tested are the replicon's resistance positions, and the label routes RAS-positive 1a patients to 16 weeks plus ribavirin on this basis. Not scored as regulatory_reliance because a trial was still required; the model chose the subgroup, not the approval.
efficacy.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 cells; genotype 1a/1b and patient-derived NS5A hybrid replicons)
efficacy.note: Baseline polymorphisms at the replicon-defined positions M28/Q30/L31/Y93 cut elbasvir/grazoprevir SVR12 from 98% to 70%; the label now mandates NS5A testing before 12-week therapy.
efficacy.quote: In genotype 1a-infected subjects, the presence of one or more HCV NS5A amino acid polymorphisms at position M28, Q30, L31, or Y93 was associated with reduced efficacy of ZEPATIER for 12 weeks (Table 11)

patient_trials.quote: Without baseline NS5A polymorphism (M28, Q30, L31, or Y93) 98% (441/450); With baseline NS5A polymorphism 70% (39/56)

efficacy.reason: Replicon RAS map picks who fails

efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.note: A multiscale viral-kinetic model fitted to Gao 2010 daclatasvir kinetics inferred two modes of action and a 45-min HCV half-life; no prediction compared yet.
efficacy.short: Kinetic model fitted to daclatasvir patients
efficacy.quote: Here, we show that understanding the effects of daclatasvir in vivo requires a multiscale model that incorporates drug effects on the HCV intracellular lifecycle, and we validated this approach with in vitro HCV infection experiments.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 23431163, PMC3593898). The model was fitted to patient data, so it is an opener, not a comparison; the two-mode prediction was validated in vitro, not in patients.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for the in-silico track at its first NS5A-class use. Fitting to patient kinetics predicts nothing testable in patients, so untested; the same Dahari/Uprichard/Cotler program later ran the model prospectively (Etzion 2020), which is why the track exists.
efficacy.model: HCV viral-kinetic mathematical model (Perelson/Dahari lineage) fitted to on-treatment serum HCV RNA decline; later run in real time to set per-patient DAA duration

efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.note: Fitted after the fact to 58 patients on sofosbuvir + daclatasvir, simeprevir or ledipasvir, the model projected cure by 6-13 weeks for all and flagged the one relapser as under-treated.
efficacy.short: Retrofit projects cure times, flags relapser
efficacy.quote: The modeling suggested that the patient who relapsed would have benefitted from an additional week of sofosbuvir+ledipasvir.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 26907973). The abstract says the analysis was retrospective but not whether fits were blind to SVR; retrodiction stands on the stated design. Canini 2017 (PLoS One, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0187409) repeated the retrofit for daclatasvir + asunaprevir (89/95 cured; 6-8 weeks projected) with no status change.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: 12-week SVR outcomes were known before the model was fitted. It reproduced them (all projected cured within the course; the single sofosbuvir/ledipasvir relapse projected to need one more week), so retro, patient-level. The shortening projections were not tested in these patients.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: model-projected time to cure (<=13 weeks for all 58) vs SVR in 57/58 on 12-week sofosbuvir + daclatasvir/ledipasvir/simeprevir
efficacy.model: HCV viral-kinetic mathematical model (Perelson/Dahari lineage) fitted to on-treatment serum HCV RNA decline; later run in real time to set per-patient DAA duration

efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.note: Real-time modeling of week 0-4 kinetics shortened therapy in 11/29 patients on velpatasvir-, elbasvir- or ledipasvir-based regimens; SVR 28/29, the one relapse a 6-week sofosbuvir/velpatasvir patient.
efficacy.quote: Real-time mathematical modeling of early HCV kinetics can be utilized for shortening DAAs duration in approximately 40% of patients without compromising treatment efficacy.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 33082372, PMC7575564). Regimens named in the companion paper Dasgupta 2020 (doi:10.1093/infdis/jiaa219): sofosbuvir-velpatasvir, elbasvir-grazoprevir, sofosbuvir-ledipasvir. NCT03603327 has no posted results, so registry_date is the first-posting date. Single-arm pilot, n=29, 11 shortened.
efficacy.judgement: First prospective prediction on this track: the model chose, in real time, which patients could stop early (patient-level). 10/11 shortened patients were cured as predicted; the one relapse was a model-shortened sofosbuvir/velpatasvir patient, so the patient-level call is partial, but the primary endpoint (SVR 97%) held and the source calls it a success. Scored same, not contra, because the prediction was the preserved cure rate, which held; the miss is recorded here.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: SVR 28/29 (97%) overall and 10/11 in model-shortened patients vs the model's prediction of cure at the shortened duration

patient_trials.quote: Treatment duration was shortened in 11 of the 29 patients (38%). SVR was achieved in 28 of the 29 patients (97%).

efficacy.model: HCV viral-kinetic mathematical model (Perelson/Dahari lineage) fitted to on-treatment serum HCV RNA decline; later run in real time to set per-patient DAA duration

efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.note: TK-NOG humanized-liver mice (Osaka/CIEA, not the Hiroshima uPA/SCID line) were infected with serum from a ledipasvir/sofosbuvir failure carrying NS5A-P32del.
efficacy.short: P32del patient virus into TK-NOG mice
efficacy.quote: We inoculated human hepatocyte chimeric mice with sera from a patient with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir therapy failure carrying a genotype 1b HCV with NS5A L31M and P32del or from a DAA-naïve patient carrying wild-type virus.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 30684016). Host strain (TK-NOG) is from the paper's keywords and the CIEA co-author, not from a methods read.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from hcv-chimeric-upa-scid-mouse: a different humanized-liver host (TK-NOG, Osaka/CIEA) carrying a different inoculum (patient-derived P32del virus) and making a different, patient-level prediction (which retreatment a P32del failure can respond to). Osawa 2019 (J Gen Virol) used the Hiroshima uPA/SCID system and belongs on the existing track.
efficacy.model: TK-NOG human-liver chimeric mouse (CIEA) inoculated with patient-derived genotype 1b HCV carrying NS5A L31M + P32del from a ledipasvir/sofosbuvir failure

efficacy.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
efficacy.note: Mice carrying the patient's P32del virus stayed viraemic on ledipasvir plus a nucleotide NS5B inhibitor, reproducing the donor's ledipasvir/sofosbuvir relapse, but cleared on simeprevir + nucleotide or interferon.
efficacy.short: P32del mice relapse on ledipasvir, as patient did
efficacy.quote: The virus was resistant to the ledipasvir/GS-558093 (a nucleotide analog inhibitor of NS5B polymerase) regimen but susceptible to either simeprevir plus GS-558093 or peg-interferon alfa-2b, compared to the wild-type virus.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The patient side is the serum donor's own ledipasvir/sofosbuvir failure as the paper states it, plus Uemura 2019 (J Gastroenterol, doi:10.1007/s00535-018-01543-9, epub 2019-01-05): 3/3 GLE/PIB retreatment failures carried NS5A-P32del. Both were public before this paper (epub 2019-01-25), so the mouse reproduced a known result.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the inoculum came from a patient who had already failed ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, and P32del failure on NS5A-inhibitor regimens was in print (Uemura 2019) twenty days earlier. The mouse reproduced it, so retro, patient-level. Its forward prediction (NS5A-free two-drug combinations cure P32del) has no patient test I could find; Mawatari 2020 adds one more P32del GLE/PIB failure, consistent but not a test, so no later entry.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: persistent serum HCV RNA on ledipasvir/GS-558093 in P32del mice vs the donor patient's ledipasvir/sofosbuvir relapse
efficacy.model: TK-NOG human-liver chimeric mouse (CIEA) inoculated with patient-derived genotype 1b HCV carrying NS5A L31M + P32del from a ledipasvir/sofosbuvir failure

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. model_first_use_year 2007 is the earliest GLP study initiation date in the FDA Daklinza pharmacology review (phototoxicity study DS07109, June 2007); the repeat-dose studies are undated in the text I read.
safety.judgement: Opener uses the first patient tolerability report as proxy; the toxicology package itself was not public until the 2015 FDA review.
safety.model: Repeat-dose toxicology in rodent and non-rodent (mouse/rat, dog, monkey)
safety.note: Toxicology-cleared doses to 100 mg were tolerated for 14 days with placebo-like adverse events; no animal-to-patient comparison yet published.
safety.short: MAD doses tolerated; no comparison yet
safety.quote: BMS-790052 was well tolerated in all dose groups, with adverse events occurring with a similar frequency in BMS-790052- and placebo-treated groups.

safety.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
safety.confidence_note: Read in the bundled review text (p. 7 and the safety-pharmacology section). The same review states 'No clear target organs of toxicity were identified in repeat-dose toxicology studies in mice, rats and dogs'.
safety.judgement: The model's silence (no target organ; no cardiovascular signal in dog telemetry) was not contradicted in patients, and the reviewer states the comparison. Ombitasvir's review (Viekira Pak, Dec 2014) makes the same no-target-organ statement; one entry suffices.
safety.model: Repeat-dose toxicology in rodent and non-rodent (mouse/rat, dog, monkey)
safety.note: Ledipasvir: no target organ in mouse, rat or dog, hERG and dog telemetry silent; FDA states no haemodynamic or ECG effects in trials.
safety.quote: No significant hemodynamic or electrocardiographic heart effects have been observed in clinical trials with LDV.

safety.magnitude_basis: adrenal cortical hypertrophy/hyperplasia predicted in rat and monkey; cortisol unchanged in patients
safety.population: Unselected (all HCV genotypes; genotype and baseline NS5A RAS subgroups noted per entry)
safety.confidence_note: Read in the bundled summary review; the exposure margin is from the pharmacology review (6-month rat adrenal vacuolation at AUC >= 9.14 ug.h/mL; 1-month rat NOAEL AUC 5.07 ug.h/mL) against a human 60-mg AUC of roughly 11 ug.h/mL that I recall from the label PK table but did not re-read.
safety.judgement: Scored contra by the letter of the rule: a predicted harm at or near clinical exposure that never appeared in patients is a wrong prediction (magnitude opposite). A lenient read is 'same' (the animals flagged it, the clinic monitored and cleared it). The track stays contra: later no-target-organ predictions for elbasvir (2016), velpatasvir (2016) and pibrentasvir (2017) held in patients but by rule do not turn a failed track back. Daclatasvir's monkey liver findings are not scored: the clinical ALT signal was attributed to asunaprevir, a protease inhibitor outside this class.
safety.model: Repeat-dose toxicology in rodent and non-rodent (mouse/rat, dog, monkey)
safety.note: Daclatasvir: rats and monkeys showed adrenal cortical hypertrophy and raised corticosterone near clinical exposure; cortisol monitored in early trials showed nothing.
safety.short: Rat/monkey adrenal signal absent in patients
safety.quote: Adrenal activity was monitored in early clinical trials (cortisol), but no effects were noted.
